classes.name: House of Assembly general elections
classes.finest_note: The Electoral Office publishes every candidate's votes by polling station for 2014, 2016, 2019, 2021, and 2022 (JSON behind its results maps), every candidate by constituency for 2009 and 2010, and only the electorate, votes cast, and winner of each constituency from 1970 to 2005.
classes.note: Representatives are elected by first past the post in single-member constituencies (Constitution s.30(1)(a)), 11 under the Associated State constitution of 1967 and 21 since 1975. Parliament lasts five years from the first sitting of the House after a dissolution unless dissolved sooner on the Prime Minister's advice (s.54(2) and (4)), and the general election follows within three months of a dissolution (s.55(1)). The nine senators are appointed (class senators). Elections before 1967 were to the colonial Legislative Council (class legco).

classes.name: Legislative Council elections
classes.note: Until March 1967 Dominica was a Crown colony with a Governor and a Legislative Council (Electoral Office, Brief History). The elections law in force, now the House of Assembly (Elections) Act, began as Act 14 of 1951, and the Legislative Council's elected members were chosen under it until the Associated State constitution created the House of Assembly in 1967.
classes.locator: https://electoraloffice.gov.dm/about-us/brief-history ("The form of government in the Commonwealth of Dominica was Crown Colony with a Governor and a Legislative Council until March 1967 when it became an Associated State")
classes.disposition_reason: The Electoral Office publishes no result before 1970; the colonial returns are in the Dominica Official Gazette and the colonial blue books, which no official host has online.

classes.name: Senators of the House of Assembly
classes.note: Five senators are appointed on the Prime Minister's advice and four on the Leader of the Opposition's (Constitution s.34(1)). Parliament may provide that they be elected by the voters for Representatives instead (s.34(1) proviso and (2)), but the House of Assembly (Elections) Act makes no such provision.
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed, not elected: Parliament has never prescribed the election of senators that s.34(1) allows.

classes.name: Election of the President by the House of Assembly
classes.note: The President serves five years from being declared elected (s.23(1)). On a joint nomination by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition the Speaker declares the nominee elected without a vote (s.19(2)); otherwise the House elects by secret ballot, a majority of all its members being needed (s.19(4)-(5A)).
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the members of the House of Assembly by secret ballot or declared on a joint nomination (Constitution s.19); not a public election.

classes.name: Constitutional referendums
classes.note: A bill altering s.42, Schedule 1, or a provision listed in Schedule 1 needs three quarters of the elected members and then a majority of the votes cast in a referendum of the voters for Representatives, run by the Electoral Commission (s.42(2), (3)(b), (5), and (7)).
classes.disposition_reason: None held: the Electoral Office's records list no referendum since independence.

classes.name: Party candidate selection
classes.locator: https://www.dominica.gov.dm/laws/chapters/chap2-01.pdf (s.15(2): every candidate "must be nominated in writing by not less than six registered electors of the constituency")
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their candidates under their own rules; no law provides for a state-run primary.

classes.name: Roseau City Council elections
classes.finest_note: The Chief Elections Officer's notice gives each candidate's votes by ward, with turnout and the split by sex.
classes.note: Eight of the thirteen members are elected, two from each of four wards; the Minister nominates five (Roseau City Council Act s.3(2)-(3)). The council's term is three years (s.65); the first election under the Act was on 31 May 1982 (s.64). The Mayor of Roseau is the council's chairman, whom the council elects from its members (ss.10 and 11). The Act replaced an older Roseau town council whose elections are not on the Electoral Office's record. By-elections fill elected vacancies (s.35).

dates.quote: s.64: "The first election under this Act shall take place on 31st of May, 1982"; s.3(3): the city "shall be divided into four wards ... and each ward shall elect not more than two persons to the Council"

classes.note: Eight of the thirteen members are elected, two from each of four wards; the Minister nominates five (Portsmouth Town Council Act s.3(2)-(3)). classes.name: Canefield Urban Council elections
classes.finest_note: The council area, at large; results notices list each candidate's votes.
classes.note: Five of the eight members are elected by the electors of the area at large and the Minister nominates three (Canefield Urban Council Act s.3(2)); the term is about three years from the council's first meeting after a general election (s.29(1)). In 2022 the five candidates nominated were declared elected unopposed on nomination day. The next general election is set for 21 December 2026.

classes.name: Village council elections
classes.name_en: Village council general elections and by-elections
classes.finest_note: Each council's area at large; the notices give every candidate's votes, the turnout, and the split by sex.
classes.note: Each village council has elected members chosen by the residents of its village district and members nominated by the Minister, under the Village Councils Ordinance, Cap. 190 of the Revised Laws of Dominica (1961), as amended by Act 7 of 1994 (qualifications in s.5). The Chief Elections Officer runs each council's general election on its own date, with a presiding officer appointed under s.41(1), and by-elections fill vacancies. The Electoral Office's List of Village Councils names 38 village councils; it omits Salisbury, whose council held elections the Office announced, so the register is not current.

dates.note: About 150 notices from 2012 to 2016 under Village Council Elections and more than 300 news items from 2017, mixing general elections, by-elections, nominations, and appointments of officers; not yet counted by year.

classes.finest_note: The territory at large; the notice gives each candidate's votes, the rejected ballots, the turnout, and the split by sex.
classes.note: The Chief is elected by the voters registered in the Reserve (Carib Reserve Act s.3, as amended by Act 15 of 1984) and chairs the Kalinago Council. The 1978 Act continued a council that existed before it (s.14(4)) and is now cited as the Kalinago Territory Act.
